\section[śukravāsaraḥ]{\sk{शुक्रवासरः} (śukravāsaraḥ) — Friday}

\label{lesson:SA-C86-friday}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for Wednesday, then the Sanskrit for Thursday.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{शुक्रवासरः}}
\textbf{\sk{शुक्रवासरः}} (\emph{śukravāsaraḥ}) — \textquotedblleft{}Friday\textquotedblright{}, the day of \textbf{\sk{शुक्र}}, Venus.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Venus's day.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{śukravāsaraḥ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{śukravāsaraḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{śukravāsaraḥ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for Wednesday, then the Sanskrit for Thursday, then say \emph{śukravāsaraḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{शुक्रवासरः} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Friday\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[samayaḥ]{\sk{समयः} (samayaḥ) — time}

\label{lesson:SA-C86-time}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for Saturday, then the Sanskrit for Sunday.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{समयः}}
\textbf{\sk{समयः}} (\emph{samayaḥ}) — \textquotedblleft{}time\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\sk{कः} \sk{समयः}?} — \textquotedblleft{}what is the time?\textquotedblright{}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The question on every street.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{samayaḥ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{samayaḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{kaḥ samayaḥ?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for Saturday, then the Sanskrit for Sunday, then say \emph{samayaḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{समयः} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Time\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[kṣaṇaḥ]{\sk{क्षणः} (kṣaṇaḥ) — a moment}

\label{lesson:SA-C86-moment}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for Sunday, then the Sanskrit for time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{क्षणः}}
\textbf{\sk{क्षणः}} (\emph{kṣaṇaḥ}) — \textquotedblleft{}a moment\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\sk{एकः} \sk{क्षणः}} — \textquotedblleft{}one moment\textquotedblright{}, said with a raised hand.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The polite way to ask for a pause.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kṣaṇaḥ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kṣaṇaḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{ekaḥ kṣaṇaḥ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for Sunday, then the Sanskrit for time, then say \emph{kṣaṇaḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{क्षणः} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A moment\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
